placement.decision: A NEW business area, 'Islamic Account Servicing and Positions', namespace 'isb-accounts', with two business domains: 'Islamic Account Servicing' (Account, Posting, Balance, Statement) and 'Islamic Position Keeping' (Position).
whyNotInsideDepositsAndInvestmentAccount: These five must serve the WHOLE estate, not the deposit products: the Open Banking AIS surface has to list a Murabaha financing account and a Sukuk holding alongside a Mudarabah savings account. Placing the ledger inside 'Deposits and Investment Accounts' would make all twelve Islamic Financing domains and all three Sukuk domains depend on a deposits namespace to post a single entry.

In generate.py the business area IS the Kubernetes namespace (AREA_NAMESPACE, generator/generate.py:69-76). Business area is therefore a deployment and blast-radius boundary here, not only a taxonomy label. The servicing ledger is the one component every other area calls; it earns its own namespace for the same reason openbank-pkg earns its own module.

Separation of concerns that the 48 already imply: a product domain owns the CONTRACT (its terms, its ratio, its underlying asset). The servicing core owns the SERVABLE RECORD (identity, postings, balances, statements). Collapsing them means 17 product repos each grow their own ledger — the exact duplication the generator exists to prevent.
placement.whyNotInsideTakafulAndSharedOperations: That area is already the estate's catch-all (Customer Reference Data, AAOIFI Financial Accounting, IFSB Regulatory Reporting, channels). Adding the account ledger to it buries the single most-called component of the estate in a bucket named for insurance.
placement.bianAnalogue: BIAN separates per-product fulfilment service domains from position-keeping / operations service domains, which is the same split made here. I did NOT verify BIAN v12's exact business-area or service-domain names against a primary source in this session — see uncertain[] on each domain. The split is justified above on estate-internal grounds that do not depend on BIAN naming.

conventions.noDuplicationOfComplianceFields: A Shariah-bearing value has exactly ONE owning service domain. conformanceHazards.finding: OBActiveCurrencyAndAmount_SimpleType pattern is ^\d{1,13}$|^\d{1,13}\.\d{1,5}$ — no sign is permitted. Our postings and balances are SIGNED int64 minor units.
conformanceHazards.consequence: The boundary MUST split a signed int64 into (magnitude, CreditDebitIndicator). Serialising -1250 as "-12.50" is a schema violation; serialising it as "12.50" with the wrong indicator is a money error that validates. This is the conversion's most likely silent failure.
conformanceHazards.mitigation: ISB-IPO-03 and ISB-IBA-11 fix the sign/indicator agreement in the CATALOG, so the generated rule tests catch a disagreement before the Go boundary ever sees it.

conformanceHazards.finding: The same pattern caps the integer part at 13 digits.
conformanceHazards.consequence: int64 minor units reach 9.22e18. In a 0-exponent currency (JPY) any balance above 9,999,999,999,999 minor units is unrepresentable in OBIE; in a 3-exponent currency (BHD/KWD/OMR/TND/JOD) the ceiling is 10^16 minor units. The conversion must FAIL LOUDLY, never truncate or round.
'IACC-' + a dashed UUID is 41 characters and would be rejected. Our format is 'IACC-' + 32 hex = 37. Enforced by ISB-IAC-11.
A deposit-guarantee amount on a capital-at-risk Mudarabah investment account is a false statement of the same class as the CBPII FundsAvailable:true that §7 forbids. ISB-IST-13 rejects it.

Every Islamic account published on the OBIE surface carries an approximate product code. ISB-IAC-12 makes that approximation an explicit, audited, SSB-visible mapping decision (onViolation: flag) instead of a silent default.

theTwoRepresentations.java: These five control records, and the Java isb-* cores generally: SIGNED int64 MINOR units + an explicit ISO 4217 currency field alongside every amount. Never a float, never a decimal column.
theTwoRepresentations.go: openbank-pkg/obie.Amount — decimal STRING + ISO currency, over shopspring/decimal.

moneyBoundary.theExactConversionPoint: ONE function pair in openbank-pkg/obie (DESIGN.md §6: 'One conversion function … No other code may convert'), called from exactly one place per direction: openbank-islamic's adapter to the Java isb-* cores (the read path that builds islamic-account-info, profit-distributions and shariah-compliance), and the same adapter's write path if a posting is ever initiated through the OB layer. The Java side never emits a decimal string, and the Go side never does arithmetic on minor units. The handler layer must receive obie.Amount already converted — the conversion must not be reachable from a handler, a template, or a second adapter.
whatCanGoWrong: HARDCODED ×100. Every Gulf currency this estate is actually for has exponent 3 — BHD, KWD, OMR, TND, and JOD. A ×100 conversion silently divides a Bahraini dinar balance by ten. JPY (exponent 0) multiplies it by a hundred. The ISO 4217 exponent table is the only authority, and BHD must be the FIRST property-test case, not an afterthought.

SIGN LOSS. OBIE's amount pattern is unsigned (see conformanceHazards/unsignedAmount). A signed int64 must become (magnitude, CreditDebitIndicator). A wrong indicator produces a response that validates, passes the conformance suite, and is wrong by twice the amount.

TRAILING-ZERO STRIPPING. decimal.String() renders 10.00 as '10' (named in DECISIONS.md WAVE 3 as an existing defect). Converting back gives 1000 minor units in a 2-exponent currency and 10000 in a 3-exponent one if the exponent is re-derived from the string's visible decimals instead of from the currency. NEVER infer the exponent from the string.
13-DIGIT OVERFLOW. OBIE caps the integer part at 13 digits; int64 minor units go far higher. The conversion must return an error, not a truncated or rounded amount.

DOUBLE CONVERSION. minor → decimal → minor across the sibling and the OBIE surface must be exactly round-trip (property test, both directions, every exponent). Any intermediate rounding is a money leak repeated per request.

A BARE int64 CROSSING THE BOUNDARY. Which is why every money field in this fragment is required to declare currencyField, and why rules ISB-IPO-10, ISB-IBA-01 and ISB-IPS-10 reject a posting, balance or position whose currency disagrees with its account. An amount without its currency is not a number, it is a guess.

A RATIO ENTERING THE MONEY PATH. profitSharingRatio and nonCompliantIncomeRatio are int numerator/denominator pairs and must never be converted by, or routed through, the money functions. A ratio rendered as a decimal string and re-parsed is how an exact 7/10 becomes 0.7000000000000001.
moneyBoundary.whatThisFragmentDoesAboutIt: Nothing at the Go layer — that is openbank-islamic's slice. What it does do is make the catalog side non-negotiable: type 'money' is defined as signed int64 minor units with a mandatory currencyField and a *Minor name suffix (check_fragment.py asserts all three), type 'ratio' is two int columns, and no float appears anywhere in this file (asserted by the same checker).

In practice the at-risk amount of a Mudarabah IAH balance is not a stored number but a consequence of the pool's performance at a valuation date, and whether any part of a Mudarabah balance is ever 'guaranteed' (e.g. an unpaid declared-profit amount that has become a debt of the bank) is exactly the kind of question only an SSB can settle. uncertain: The AAOIFI Financial Accounting Standards that govern how IAH profit, PER/IRR and purification are PRESENTED were never obtained by this estate's research (DECISIONS.md WAVE 3 says so for takaful; the same is true here). Every money field on this statement is therefore a presentation choice, not a standard-backed line item. This is the single biggest gap in my slice.

Zakat: I carry only zakatAssessmentRef and no zakat figure. Whether a statement must disclose a zakat base or a zakat deducted amount is jurisdictional (compulsory collection in some jurisdictions, voluntary elsewhere) and I could not model it from verified sources. ISB-IST has no zakat rule as a result — a deliberate omission, not an oversight.

ISB-IST-02 assumes every balance movement is explained by a statement line in the same period. Value-dated postings that book in one period and value in another break this, and I did not model which of bookingAt or valueDate governs period membership. That choice changes the arithmetic of ISB-IST-01 and ISB-IST-02 and a reviewer must fix it before either rule is generated.

I modelled gross pool profit as an OPTIONAL disclosure (grossPoolProfitDisclosedMinor). Whether an IAH is entitled to see the pool's gross result — and not only their own share — is exactly the kind of transparency question IFSB-30 Principle 18 addresses and I could not resolve from the extracted text.

The OBIE statement surface has published code sets for Fee, Interest, Benefit, Value, Rate and Amount types, and NONE of them has a profit, purification, ta'widh or zakat member. I did not pick a UK.OBIE.* code to approximate any of them: unlike AccountTypeCode (where a value is mandatory and some code must be chosen), these are optional, so the honest action is to omit them from the OBIE response entirely and serve them on the sibling. A reviewer may prefer approximation plus disclosure; I chose omission.

uncertain: AAOIFI SS 21's screening thresholds (commonly quoted as 30/30/5) could not be verified against primary text by this estate's research, and sources disagree on the purification formula. I therefore modelled NO threshold and NO formula: screening carries a versioned, SSB-approved criteria-set reference and an outcome. A generator default here would be manufacturing authority.

Unit accounting at a declared integer scale is my invention for keeping floats out. It is correct arithmetic but I do not know whether it matches how Islamic banks actually express fractional IAH units, or whether a ratio pair would be the better representation for a unitised holding. A reviewer should check this against a real IAH product before it is generated.

Whether an IAH position should be published to TPPs at all is an open product/privacy question. I mapped the whole domain to the sibling surface, but a holdings list is materially more sensitive than a balance, and AIS v4.0.1 has no holdings resource to normalise it against.

IJARA_ASSET_INTEREST is in instrumentKind because a lessee's interest in a leased asset is a real position, but I modelled no asset-specific field (residual value, transfer-of-ownership schedule for IMB). That belongs to the Ijara Muntahia Bittamleek product domain, and I may have the boundary in the wrong place.

Corporate actions on sukuk (early call, restructuring, default/sukuk-holder recourse to the underlying asset) are folded into one CORPORATE_ACTION movement kind. Sukuk default and recourse are a serious modelling area I did not attempt.

I did not model the relationship between a position's valuation and the Balance domain's at-risk split — i.e. whether atRiskAmountMinor must equal the sum of position carrying amounts. It probably must, and a cross-domain rule would be the right place to say so, but the assert grammar has no cross-domain aggregate and I did not invent one.

areaWideGaps: THE PREREQUISITE IS STILL A PREREQUISITE. These five entries make an Open Banking surface POSSIBLE; they do not make it honest on their own. The sibling surface's ContractType, ProfitSharingRatio, PER/IRR and SSB provenance are all REFERENCES into the 48 product and governance domains, which are still byte-identical scaffolds with additionalProperties:true over a ConcurrentHashMap. Until at least the six cores named in DECISIONS.md WAVE 3 (isb-mudarabah-savings-account, isb-mudarabah-term-investment-account, isb-wakala-investment-account, isb-profit-calculation-and-distribution, isb-murabaha-financing, isb-ijara-leasing) carry real control records, openbank-islamic serves REAL account identity, postings and balances with EMPTY contract semantics. That is a better failure than today's (nothing to serve at all) but it is not a working surface.

A SHARIAH BLOCK HAS NO CONFORMANT ERROR CODE, AND THIS FRAGMENT DOES NOT FIX IT. OBError1.ErrorCode is minLength 4 / maxLength 4 drawn from OBExternalStatusReason1Code, which has no permissibility value (DECISIONS.md WAVE 1). ISB-IPO-08 records a BLOCK outcome in the ledger; it cannot express one in a conformant UK error body. The three options (reuse U014 FailsControlParameters and lie slightly, use a vendor namespace and break the 4-char constraint, or return the block only on the sibling surface) are an OPEN OWNER DECISION. My recommendation, not applied: express it ONLY on the sibling, whose error envelope is ours to define, and never on an OBIE path.

FAIL-OPEN VS FAIL-CLOSED ON AN UNSCREENABLE MOVEMENT IS UNDECIDED. ISB-IPO-13 deliberately flags rather than rejects, so the estate's honest state (most postings are NOT_SCREENED) is visible instead of silently defaulted. It does not decide the policy, because the research is explicit that the gate's only inputs — a conditional ISO 20022 Purpose code and a conditional ISO 18245 MCC — are unreliable, and 'REFER every payment' makes the demo unusable.

DESIGN.md §7's ContractType ENUM IS USABLE HERE BUT NOT COMPLETE, and I did not extend it. All ten values are used; what they cannot express is (a) Wadiah yad amanah vs yad dhamanah, which are different guarantee regimes under one value, and (b) Musharakah and Diminishing Musharakah, which the estate HAS as product domains ('Musharakah Partnership Financing', 'Diminishing Musharakah Home Finance') and which §7's list omits entirely. A Musharakah account therefore cannot be published with a truthful ContractType today. The sibling fragment isb-operations raises the same class of problem for Takaful/Retakaful/Ujrah/Tawarruq. Raised per §7's instruction, not silently diverged from.

THE AAOIFI FINANCIAL ACCOUNTING STANDARDS WERE NEVER OBTAINED by this estate's research — only the Shariah Standards (SS) were, and the IFSB standards partly. Everything in this fragment about how profit, PER/IRR, purification and unrealised movement are PRESENTED (the statement's money fields, the balance components, the withdrawable flag) is therefore a presentation choice no clause backs. This is the largest single gap in the slice and it is an obtainable one: the documents exist, nobody here has read them.

MONEY CROSSES THE BOUNDARY IN ONE DIRECTION TODAY AND TWO TOMORROW. The read path (Java int64 minor → Go decimal string → OBIE) is specified in moneyBoundary. The WRITE path (a TPP-initiated payment landing as an Islamic Posting) inverts it, and the inverse conversion is where the 13-digit ceiling and the rounding policy actually bite. DESIGN.md §6 requires one function pair with property tests; nothing in this fragment can enforce that, and no rule here will catch a Go-side conversion bug. BHD (exponent 3) must be the first test case, not JPY and not GBP.

FIVE DOMAINS IS THE MINIMUM, NOT THE SET. Two further servicing domains are arguably missing and I did not invent them, because the brief named five and because inventing more taxonomy is cheap while modelling it honestly is not: (a) an Islamic Standing Order / Scheduled Payment domain — OBIE AIS has /standing-orders, /direct-debits and /scheduled-payments endpoints that this estate can currently serve with NOTHING, and a direct debit over a capital-at-risk account raises its own questions; (b) an Islamic Beneficiary domain, for the same reason (/beneficiaries). DECISIONS.md WAVE 1 already names this as an estate-wide gap. They are the 50th and 51st catalog entries, and on this fragment's placement they belong in 'Islamic Account Servicing' at a cost of one entry each.
